sentences.text: Mixosaurus translates to "Mixed Lizard" because it represents a transitional form between eel-shaped and dolphin-shaped ichthyosaurs.
This small marine reptile measured between 73 and 100 centimeters in length and weighed from 2.2 to 5.7 kilograms.
Its anatomy featured front limbs longer than its back limbs, along with toes containing more individual bones than typical reptiles.
The animal possessed narrow jaws equipped with several sharp teeth, a configuration ideal for catching fish.
A pregnant specimen of Mixosaurus panxianensis preserved with at least 11 fetuses was described from the Middle Triassic Guanling Formation in China.
While average specimens were under a meter, the largest known individuals exceeded two meters in total length.
Fossils of Mixosaurus have been discovered near the Italy-Switzerland border and in South China.
The genus Mixosaurus was named in 1887 by George H. Baur.

In 2024, a new species, Mixosaurus luxiensis, was named by Ye-Wei Fang and coauthors, with HFUT HL-21-08-002 serving as the holotype and only known specimen found in the Upper Member of the Guanling Formation in Luxi County, Yunnan Province, China.
Mixosaurus panxianensis was discovered in the Middle Triassic of Guizhou Province, China.
Recently, Mixosauridae has been separated into Mixosaurinae and the sister group Phalarondontinae.

Several species of Mixosaurus have been declared nomen dubium because their scientific descriptions are insufficient for secure classification, including M. maotaiensis, M. helveticus, M. timorensis, M. major, and M. nordenskioeldii.
Mixosaurus belongs to the family Mixosauridae and is classified within the class Reptilia.
Mixosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic, from about 247 to 242 million years ago.
